Title: ZIPPER: Slider Gizmo
Content: Objective Move or rotate the slider to adjust its distance from the zipper tape. Location Main Menu 3D Garment Select/Move 3D Toolbar Select/Move Operation Move Create a zipper. While the Simulation is turned off, follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 3D Garment Select/Move 3D Toolbar Select/Move Click the slider. The slider is selected and its Gizmo appears. Click and drag the blue segment of the Gizmo to move the slider back and forth. Sliders cannot be moved along with Y and Z axes. Rotate With the Select/Move tool, click on the slider to access the Slider Gizmo. Click and drag the blue circle of the Gizmo to rotate on the Y axis. Click and drag the yellow-green circle of the Gizmo to rotate on the X axis. Click and drag the red circle of the Gizmo to rotate on the Z axis. The selected zipper slider rotates based on the selected circle. To rotate the puller only, click on the puller while the slider is selected. The selected puller is highlighted in yellow and the Gizmo changes accordingly. Rotate the puller referencing #2. Note: To reset the slider's position and angle, right click on the slider and select the Reset Slider Arrangement option.

Title: Create Buttons along Pattern Outline
Content: Objective Create buttons along a Pattern Outline in a constant interval and distance. Location Main Menu Materials Button Button 3D toolbar Button Operation Create Select the tool/menu indicated. Right-click on the outline of the pattern. The button/buttonhole creation option window appears along the pattern outline. Note: Hold down the Shift key and left-click on a segment to select multiple. Set each option and click OK. Type Start Position Repeatedly create a button based on the starting point. Distribute Create by aligning buttons at regular intervals between the starting and ending points. Based on Start Start Position Distance Adjust the distance between the clicked segment and the center of the button. Interval Adjust the spacing between the pattern outline and the center of the button. Reverse The starting point of the button and replicated created direction are adjusted in reverse. Replicate Interval Adjust the distance between the buttons. Number of Buttons/Buttonholes Adjust the number of buttons. Distribute (ver. 11) Position Distance Adjust the distance between the clicked segment and t he center of the button. Start/End Interval Adjust the spacing between the pattern outline and the center of the start/end buttons. Replicate Number of Buttons/Buttonholes Enter the number of buttons/buttonholes to align between the start and end points. A group button is created. Select Select the tool/menu indicated. Click a button or segment created along the pattern outline. All grouped buttons are selected. Change the button properties and style or right-click. Applied to grouped buttons. Group information is not copied/pasted. Note: If clicking again on the selected group button, it is able to select a button individually. Grouped buttons cannot be moved. Unlink Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. After right-clicking on a button or segment created along the pattern outline and click Unlink Buttons/Buttonholes. The group is unlinked.

Title: Show/Hide Buttonhole
Content: Objective Show or hide all buttons and buttonholes. Location 3D Window 3D Garment Display (Mouse-over) Show Button Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Window 3D Garment Display (Mouse-over) Show Button All buttons and buttonholes are now being hidden. Follow the indicated guideline once again. All hidden buttons and buttonholes are now being displayed.

Title: BUTTONHOLE STYLE PROPERTIES: Buttonhole Name
Content: Objective Rename buttonholes as desired. Location Object Browser Buttonhole Tab Property Editor Change Name Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Buttonhole Tab Property Editor Change Name Type in the desired name. The name is now being edited and applied.

Title: Buttonhole Right-Click Menus
Content: Objective Change status of buttonholes as desired. Location 3D Toolbar Select/Move Button Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D/2D Buttonhole) Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar Select/Move Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D/2D Buttonhole) Operation Follow the indicated guideline: 3D Toolbar Select/Move Button Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D/2D Buttonhole) Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar Select/Move Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D/2D Buttonhole) Right-click on the buttonhole to edit. Buttonhole related pop-up menu appears. Pop-up Menu Description Reset 3D Position Reset to location of pre-simulation. Copy Copy the selected buttonhole. Paste Paste the selected buttonhole. Mirror Paste (Position Only) Mirror paste the position of the selected buttonhole. Delete Delete the selected buttonhole. Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern Duplicate the selected buttonhole to its symmetric pattern. Activate/Deactivate Activate or deactivate the selected buttonhole. Freeze/Unfreeze Freeze or unfreeze the selected buttonhole. Set Number of Sewing Layers Set the number of sewing layers for the selected buttonhole. After setting the Number of Sewing Layers, use the Select/Move Button tool to adjust buttonholes' locations on each Patterns. Flip Move the selected buttonhole to the opposite side. Align Align selected buttonholes based on the selected options. Distribute Distribute selected buttonholes horizontally or vertically with same intervals.

Title: ADD CUSTOM BUTTON AND BUTTONHOLE: Register Custom Image as Buttonhole
Content: Objective Register a custom image as a buttonhole. Location Main Menu Materials Button Register Buttonhole Object Browser Buttonhole Tab Select a Buttonhole Style Property Editor Shape plus button Operation Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu Materials Button Register Buttonhole Object Browser Buttonhole Tab Select a Buttonhole Style Property Editor Shape plus button The Create Buttonhole window appears. Enter its name in the Name field. Click the plus button button next to the Image option. The File Browser appears. Select an image to be used as a buttonhole. Fill in all required fields and click OK. Registered buttonhole is automatically added to Property Editor Shape. Registered buttonhole is saved in Marvelous Designer Assets_ver.x.x.xx Preferences Buttons_Preset.

Title: Move Buttonhole
Content: Objective Move buttonholes as desired. Location Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button 3D Window Toolbar Select/Move Button Operation Move Buttonholes with Click-and-Drag Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button 3D Window Toolbar Select/Move Button Click and drag the buttonholes to the desired location on either of 2D or 3D Pattern. The selected buttonholes are now being moved accordingly. Note: Move multiple buttonholes at once by selecting them in the 2D window (ver2.4.0). Move Buttonholes with Distance Input (ver2.5.0) Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button 3D Window Toolbar Select/Move Button While click-and-dragging the buttonholes with left-click mouse button, click right-click mouse button in either of 2D or 3D window. The Moving Distance window appears. Enter desired value in the menu. Distance Moved Sets the moved distance of the buttonhole from its original location. Position Sets the position of the center of the buttonhole from the left/right/top/bottom of the pattern outline. Click OK. The buttonholes are now being moved according to the input value. Note: Buttonholes can only be moved within the boundaries of the Pattern.

Title: Create Buttonhole
Content: Objective Create buttonholes and place them as desired. Location Main Menu Materials Button Buttonhole 3D Toolbar Buttonhole Operation Create Buttonhole Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Button Buttonhole 3D Toolbar Buttonhole Click on a desired point on the 3D Garment or 2D Pattern. A buttonhole is created. Enter the number of garment layers and click OK. The buttonholes are now being created. Input Measurement for Buttonhole Position Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Button Buttonhole 3D Toolbar Buttonhole Right-click on the 2D pattern where buttonholes would be placed. The Moving Distance window appears. Input desired measurements for accurate placement. Placement preview depending on the input value displays along the mouse in the 2D window. Click OK to place. The buttonholes are now being created.

Title: BUTTONHOLE STYLE PROPERTIES: Buttonhole Size
Content: Objective Adjust buttonhole sizes as desired. Location Object Browser Buttonhole Tab Property Editor Size Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Buttonhole Tab Property Editor Size Type in the desired size value. The buttonhole size is now being adjusted and applied.

Title: ADD CUSTOM BUTTON AND BUTTONHOLE: Register Custom OBJ as Button
Content: Objective Register a custom OBJ file as Button. Location Main Menu Materials Button Register Button Property Editor Shape plus_button.png Operation Create Button OBJ Please check below requirements before registering an OBJ as a button. Required: Position the face of an OBJ towards Y-axis. Position the contact point of an OBJ where it should be attached to 3D garments at 0,0,0 (x,y,z) coordinates. The unit of OBJs must be in mm. Recommended: Please maintain the number of vertices of an OBJ below 1000 to avoid speed issues. The distance between an OBJ and the ground should be 0. (You can adjust the distance in Marvelousdesigner. Button Property Setting Thread Length (cm)) Register Button OBJ Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. Register Button window appears. After setting the following options, Click OK. Name Set the name of the button file. Thumbnail Apply the thumbnail of the button file. Button (ver. 11) Set the properties for the button file to be registered. Note: If the OBJ shape is different for each button size, click the + button on the top right to register as buttons of various sizes. Size Name Set the size name. OBJ Load the OBJ file to be registered with the button. Width/Thickness/Weight Set the width/thickness/weight of the button. Default Size Set the size to be applied by default when changing with the button. The registered button is saved in the path below. Assets Materials Hardware_and_Trims Button &amp Buttonhole Button Create Button OBJ by Thread Type Set the Mesh name of the button to REN_BUTTON, REN_THREAD. Create an OBJ for each thread type with the above MESH name. Set the name of the OBJ file for each thread type to *_Cross.obj, *_Parallel.obj , *_Square.obj. Register the created OBJ file as a button. Save the created *_Cross.btn, *_Parallel.btn , *_Square.btn files in the path below. C:UsersPublicDocumentsMarvelousdesignerAssetsMaterialsHardware_and_TrimsButton &amp ButtonholeButton Run Marvelousdesigner and change the type of the thread in the button property window &gt Type &gt Thread Type.

Title: BUTTONHOLE STYLE PROPERTIES: Buttonhole Material
Content: Objective Change color of buttonholes as desired. Location Object Browser Buttonhole Tab Property Editor Material Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Buttonhole Tab Property Editor Material Adjust the color, material type, and opacity.

Title: BUTTONHOLE STYLE PROPERTIES: Buttonhole Shape
Content: Objective Change buttonhole shapes as desired. Location Object Browser Buttonhole Tab Property Editor Shape Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Buttonhole Tab Property Editor Shape Click the drop down menu on the right. Preset buttonhole shapes appear in the menu. Select a desired buttonhole shape. The buttonhole shape is now being replaced. All other relevant buttonholes are also being replaced.

Title: Copy/Paste Buttonhole
Content: Objective Copy and paste multiple buttonholes with keeping the interval space evenly. Location Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar Select/Move Button Operation Copy/Paste Buttonhole Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar Select/Move Button Right click on an existing buttonhole, then select Copy (Ctrl+C) from the pop-up menu. Right click again, then select Paste (Ctrl+V) from the pop-up menu. Click on a desired place to locate the copy of the buttonhole. Input Interval/Number/Position to Copy/Pase Buttonhole Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar Select/Move Button Right click on an existing buttonhole, then select Copy (Ctrl+C) from the pop-up menu. Right click again, then select Paste (Ctrl+V) from the pop-up menu. Right click on a desired place to locate the copy of the buttonhole. The Paste window appears. Input desired value for interval/number of buttonholes/position. Interval Sets the distance between buttonholes. Number of Buttons/Buttonholes Sets the number of buttonholes to copy/paste. Position Sets the position of the center of the copied button/buttonhole from the left/right/top/bottom of the pattern outline (ver2.5.0). Click OK. The buttonholes are now being created and applied accordingly.

Title: Copy Buttonhole Style
Content: Objective Copy and modify a buttonhole in order to create a new buttonhole style or adjust its properties. Location Object Browser Buttonhole Tab Copy Operation Navigate to the Object Browser and select an item in the buttonhole tab. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Buttonhole Tab Copy A new buttonhole item with the same properties of the selected item is now being created.

Title: Apply Buttonhole Style
Content: Objective Apply buttonhole styles or fabric material (.zfab) onto buttonholes as desired. Location Object Browser Buttonhole Tab Operation Apply Buttonhole Style In Property Editor Click on a buttonhole and select a buttonhole style in the Property Editor. The selected buttonhole style is now being applied to the buttonhole. Select A Buttonhole And Apply Buttonhole Style Select a buttonhole. Follow the indicated guideline: Object Browser Buttonhole Tab Assigned to Selected Patterns The buttonhole style is now being applied to the selected buttonhole. Select A Buttonhole And Apply A New Buttonhole Style Select a buttonhole. Follow the indicated guideline: Object Browser Buttonhole Tab Assigned to New Fabric A new buttonhole style is now being added to the buttonhole list window and applied at the same time.

Title: Buttonhole List Window
Content: It is possible to create, copy, apply and set a style in Buttonhole list window. Without any extra setting, the Default Buttonhole is applied as default. Once the Default Buttonhole style is modified, it lasts until rerun of the program and it is unable to be deleted.

Title: Reset Buttonhole Style Property
Content: Objective Reset buttonhole item properties to default value (ver2.5.0). Location Object Browser Buttonhole Tab Right-Click Buttonhole Item Pop-Up Menu Reset Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Buttonhole Tab Right-Click Buttonhole Item Pop-Up Menu Reset The buttonhole item properties are now being reset back to default value.

Title: Delete Buttonhole Style
Content: Objective Delete unnecessary buttonhole styles. Location Object Browser Buttonhole Tab Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Buttonhole Tab Select a buttonhole style to be deleted. Press the Delete key on keyboard or right click on the buttonhole style and select Delete. The selected buttonhole style is deleted.

Title: Duplicate as Button to Symmetric Pattern
Content: Objective Duplicate buttons as buttonholes, or buttonholes as buttons, to its Symmetric Pattern. Location Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar Select/Move Button Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar Select/Move Button Click on the button or buttonhole to be duplicated to its Symmetric Pattern. The selected button or buttonhole is highlighted in yellow. Right click on the selected button or buttonhole. The right-click pop-up menu appears. Depending on the selected item, select Duplicate as Button to Symmetric Pattern or Duplicate as Buttonhole to Symmetric Pattern. The selected button or buttonhole is duplicated as a buttonhole or button, depending on the selected item, to its Symmetric Pattern.

Title: Mirror Paste Buttonhole
Content: Objective Copy and mirror paste buttonholes (ver2.5.0). Location Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button Buttonhole Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R) 3D Toolbar Select/Move Button Buttonhole Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R) Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button Buttonhole Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R) 3D Toolbar Select/Move Button Buttonhole Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R) Click Copy (Ctrl+C) from the pop-up menu. Right click on the copied buttonhole then click Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R) from the pop-up menu. Placement preview displays along the mouse in the 2D window. Click on a desired location to paste the buttonholes. Note: Before pasting buttonholes in place, right click to access the Paste window where specific interval and number of buttonholes can be manually input for multiple copy-and-paste. When buttonholes are mirror-pasted, only locations are mirrored whereas other properties, such as Angle, are not.

Title: Create 2D Buttonhole Measurement
Content: Objective View buttonhole position from the pattern outline with 2D measurements (ver2.5.0). Location Object Browser Buttonhole Property Editor 2D Measurements To Center Operation Select a buttonhole with Select/Move Button tool in the 3D toolbar. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Buttonhole Property Editor 2D Measurements To Center Select the desired 2D measurement options of the Left/Right/Up/Down. The 2D measurement is now being displayed or hidden accordingly.

Title: Create Additional Buttonhole Style
Content: Objective Create a new buttonhole style. Location Object Browser Buttonhole Tab Add Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Buttonhole Tab Add A new item named after 'Buttonhole 1, 2' is now being created and applied.

Title: CREATE CUSTOM BUTTON TEXTURE: Create Button Texture
Content: Objective Create and apply custom textures to buttons in CLO in order to express various button styles. Note: Adobe Photoshop is needed to create custom button texture. Operation Download custom button texture templates (.psd) provided in the Library window: Note: Choose your desired button design and download respective custom button texture file as needed. Open downloaded .psd file in Adobe Photoshop. The template is divided into three parts each representing front, back, and thread of the button. Open a texture image to be embedded to the template. The texture will open in a new tab in Adobe Photoshop. Follow the path: Main Menu Edit Define Pattern The selected texture will be added as a pattern in Adobe Photoshop. In the Layer Window, select the desired layer to be painted with the defined pattern. The Layer Window is located along the right side of the Adobe Photoshop Window. While the desired layer is selected, left click on the Paint tool and select the defined pattern The selected layer will be painted with the chosen pattern. Hide UV and Test layers, then save the image. Note: Saving the image in .jpeg format is recommended.

Title: Move Fastened Button/Buttonhole
Content: Objective Move a fastened button only, or a button and buttonhole together. Location Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar Select/Move Button Operation Move Fastened Button Only Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar Select/Move Button Click and drag the desired button in the 2D or 3D window. The selected button is moved to where the mouse is released. The moved button stays fastened. Move Fastened Button and Buttonhole Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar Select/Move Button Hold down Shift on the keyboard, then click all buttons and buttonholes to be moved in the 2D or 3D window. Click and drag the selected buttons and buttonholes. The selected buttons and buttonholes are moved to where the mouse is released. The moved buttons and buttonholes stay fastened.

Title: Fasten/Unfasten Button
Content: Objective Fasten or unfasten buttons to style the Garment as desired. Location Main Menu Materials Button Fasten Button 3D Toolbar Fasten Button Operation Fasten Button Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Button Fasten Button 3D Toolbar Fasten Button Click on a button, then click on its corresponding buttonhole in either the 2D or 3D environment, then continue on to the remaining buttons and buttonholes. The buttons move above the buttonholes. Lock icons next to the 3D buttons and buttonholes appear (ver2.5.0). Unfasten Button Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Button Fasten Button 3D Toolbar Fasten Button Click on fastened buttons and buttonholes in either the 2D or 3D environment. Buttons are now unfastened and return to their previous location. Lock icons next to the 3D buttons and buttonholes disappear (ver2.5.0). Note: To fasten multiple buttons and buttonholes at once, click and drag in the 2D window to select all buttons to be fastened, then click the first buttonhole to be paired with the buttons (ver4.0.0). To unlock multiple buttons and buttonholes, click and drag on all fastened buttons and buttonholes. Fastened buttons and buttonholes can now be moved (ver4.0.0).

Title: BUTTON STYLE PROPERTIES: Button Size
Content: Objective Adjust button sizes as desired. Location Before ver4.0.0 Object Browser Button Tab Property Editor Size After ver4.0.0 Object Browser Button Tab Property Editor Width/ Thickness/ Weight Operation Before ver4.0.0 Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Select a button item in the Button Tab. Its properties appear in the Property Editor. Find the Size option and enter desired value. The button size is now being adjusted and applied. After ver4.0.0 Navigate to the Object Browser and select the desired Button item from the button tab. The selected button item's properties appear in the Property Editor. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Button Tab Property Editor Width/ Thickness/ Weight Refer to the table below and adjust each option as needed. Option Description Width Adjust button width. Thickness Enter the desired value for button thickness. Weight Enter the desired value for button weight in grams.

Title: BUTTON STYLE PROPERTIES: Button Name
Content: Objective Rename buttons as desired. Location Object Browser Button Tab Property Editor Change Name Operation Object Browser Select a button item in the Button Tab. Its properties appear in the Property Editor. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor Name Change Name The name is now being edited and applied.

Title: BUTTON STYLE PROPERTIES: Button Shape
Content: Objective Change button shapes as desired. Location Object Browser Button Tab Property Editor Shapes Operation Object Browser Select a button item in the Buttonhole Tab. Its properties appear in the Property Editor. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor Shapes Drop-down menu on the right hand side Preset button shapes appear in the menu. Select a desired button shape. The button shape is now being replaced. All other relevant buttons are also being replaced.

Title: BUTTON STYLE PROPERTIES: Button Material
Content: Objective Change color and texture of buttons as desired. Location Object Browser Button Tab Property Editor Material Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Button Tab Property Editor Material Adjust the texture, color, gloss , and opacity as desired.

Title: BUTTON STYLE PROPERTIES: Button Thread Material (Above ver4.2.0)
Content: Objective Change Button Thread's type, color, and material. Location Type Object Browser Button Tab Property Editor Thread Type Material Object Browser Button Tab Property Editor Material Thread Tab Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Button Tab Property Editor Thread Type Refer to below table and choose the desired Thread Type. Cross Parallel Square To apply a different material to the Button Thread, toggle off Use Same Material as Button. Configure the Button Thread's texture, color, glossiness, and opacity.
